spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od1m3p1t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

(* Two allocator instances share one runway-clearance record.  A leader is  *)
(* elected among them and only the current-epoch leader may commit a         *)
(* clearance update.  A failed leader steps down and a fresh election bumps   *)
(* the epoch, so a stale instance can never silently overwrite a clearance.   *)

CONSTANT MaxClr

Instances == {"north", "south"}
NoLeader  == "none"

VARIABLES leader, epoch, committed, acked, nextClr

vars == << leader, epoch, committed, acked, nextClr >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ leader \in Instances \cup {NoLeader}
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxClr
    /\ committed \subseteq (1..MaxClr)
    /\ acked \subseteq (1..MaxClr)
    /\ nextClr \in 1..(MaxClr + 1)

Init ==
    /\ leader = NoLeader
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ committed = {}
    /\ acked = {}
    /\ nextClr = 1

Elect(i) ==
    /\ leader = NoLeader
    /\ leader' = i
    /\ epoch' = IF epoch < MaxClr THEN epoch + 1 ELSE epoch
    /\ UNCHANGED << committed, acked, nextClr >>

Failover(i) ==
    /\ leader = i
    /\ leader' = NoLeader
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, committed, acked, nextClr >>

Commit(i) ==
    /\ leader = i
    /\ nextClr <= MaxClr
    /\ committed' = committed \cup {nextClr}
    /\ nextClr' = nextClr + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << leader, epoch, acked >>

Report(c) ==
    /\ c \in committed
    /\ c \notin acked
    /\ acked' = acked \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED << leader, epoch, committed, nextClr >>

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Elect(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Failover(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Commit(i)
    \/ \E c \in 1..MaxClr : Report(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* No clearance is ever reported to a tower unless it truly sits in the       *)
(* shared record: every acknowledged update survives in the committed set.    *)
NoLostUpdate == acked \subseteq committed
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANT MaxClr = 4
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator runs as two independent instances, "north" and
"south", that share one runway-clearance record (a single pool of clearance
ids). To keep the shared record consistent the instances run leader election
with failover: at most one instance is the leader at a time, and each election
increments a leadership epoch. Towers submit clearance requests; only the
current leader may commit a clearance into the shared record, and a clearance is
reported back to the requesting tower only after it is durably committed.

The system takes four kinds of steps. Elect(i): when there is no leader, an
instance i becomes leader and the epoch advances. Failover(i): the current
leader i detects it can no longer make progress and steps down, leaving no
leader until the next election. Commit(i): the leader i writes the next clearance
id into the shared committed record. Report(c): a clearance id c that is present
in the committed record is acknowledged back to the tower that requested it.

Because a stepped-down instance loses leadership before a new one is elected,
and because only committed clearances are ever reported, no acknowledged
clearance can be silently dropped or overwritten by a stale instance.

SAFETY PROPERTY: every clearance id that has been reported (acknowledged) back
to a tower is present in the shared committed record, so no acknowledged update
to the shared record is ever lost.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od3m2p6t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

(* An interbank settlement batch runs two-phase commit over three member      *)
(* banks.  Each batch round the coordinator authorizes members; only a member *)
(* authorized in the CURRENT round may vote to prepare, and only a prepared   *)
(* member may apply the settlement.  Authorizations from earlier rounds are    *)
(* stale: a slow member carrying an old authorization must re-authorize before *)
(* it can act again.  Members may be slow but never crash.                     *)

CONSTANT MaxRound

Members == {"boa", "citi", "wells"}

VARIABLES round, authRound, prepared, committed, phase

vars == << round, authRound, prepared, committed, phase >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ round \in 0..MaxRound
    /\ authRound \in [Members -> 0..MaxRound]
    /\ prepared \subseteq Members
    /\ committed \subseteq Members
    /\ phase \in {"open", "closed"}

Init ==
    /\ round = 0
    /\ authRound = [m \in Members |-> 0]
    /\ prepared = {}
    /\ committed = {}
    /\ phase = "open"

\* Coordinator grants a current-round authorization to member m.
Authorize(m) ==
    /\ phase = "open"
    /\ authRound' = [authRound EXCEPT ![m] = round]
    /\ UNCHANGED << round, prepared, committed, phase >>

\* A member votes to prepare, but only if its authorization is current.
Vote(m) ==
    /\ phase = "open"
    /\ authRound[m] = round
    /\ m \notin prepared
    /\ prepared' = prepared \cup {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED << round, authRound, committed, phase >>

\* A prepared member applies the settlement.
Apply(m) ==
    /\ phase = "open"
    /\ m \in prepared
    /\ m \notin committed
    /\ committed' = committed \cup {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED << round, authRound, prepared, phase >>

Close ==
    /\ phase = "open"
    /\ phase' = "closed"
    /\ UNCHANGED << round, authRound, prepared, committed >>

\* Open a fresh round; per-round votes reset but stale authorizations persist.
NewRound ==
    /\ phase = "closed"
    /\ round' = IF round < MaxRound THEN round + 1 ELSE round
    /\ prepared' = {}
    /\ committed' = {}
    /\ phase' = "open"
    /\ UNCHANGED authRound

Next ==
    \/ \E m \in Members : Authorize(m)
    \/ \E m \in Members : Vote(m)
    \/ \E m \in Members : Apply(m)
    \/ Close
    \/ NewRound

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* No stale or unauthorized member ever applies the settlement: every member  *)
(* that has committed carries an authorization issued in the current round.    *)
NoStaleAction == \A m \in committed : authRound[m] = round
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANT MaxRound = 3
INVARIANT NoStaleAction
nl:
A bank's interbank settlement batch is applied using two-phase commit across
three member banks ("boa", "citi", "wells"). The batch proceeds in rounds. In
each round the coordinator authorizes members; an authorization is stamped with
the round number in which it was granted. Only a member whose authorization
matches the current round may vote to prepare, and only a prepared member may
apply (commit) the settlement. Members can be slow — they may lag arbitrarily
between authorization, voting, and applying — but they never fail outright.

The system takes these steps. Authorize(m): the coordinator grants member m a
current-round authorization. Vote(m): a member m whose authorization is current
and that has not yet prepared votes to prepare. Apply(m): a prepared member m
applies the settlement into the committed set. Close: the coordinator closes the
current round. NewRound: after a round is closed the coordinator opens the next
round, resetting the per-round prepared and committed sets while the members'
prior authorizations persist and thereby become stale.

Because voting requires a current-round authorization and the committed set is
cleared at every new round, a member carrying only an old (stale) authorization
cannot prepare or apply until it re-authorizes in the new round.

SAFETY PROPERTY: every member that has applied the settlement in the committed
set holds an authorization issued in the current round, so no stale or
unauthorized member ever performs a settlement action.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od6m8p4t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

(* An elevator bank in a skyscraper admits passengers into two cars under a    *)
(* hierarchical locking discipline: an agent first takes the coarse bank lock, *)
(* then a fine per-car lock, and only then boards a waiting request into that   *)
(* car.  Boarding requests may be serviced in any order (messages reordered).  *)
(* The whole bank has a fixed occupancy ceiling that boarding must respect.     *)

CONSTANTS BankCap, MaxReq

Agents == {"a1", "a2"}
Cars   == {"c1", "c2"}
Free   == "free"

VARIABLES coarse, fine, load, pending, served

vars == << coarse, fine, load, pending, served >>

TotalLoad == load["c1"] + load["c2"]

TypeOK ==
    /\ coarse \in Agents \cup {Free}
    /\ fine \in [Cars -> Agents \cup {Free}]
    /\ load \in [Cars -> Nat]
    /\ pending \subseteq (1..MaxReq)
    /\ served \subseteq (1..MaxReq)

Init ==
    /\ coarse = Free
    /\ fine = [c \in Cars |-> Free]
    /\ load = [c \in Cars |-> 0]
    /\ pending = 1..MaxReq
    /\ served = {}

AcquireCoarse(a) ==
    /\ coarse = Free
    /\ coarse' = a
    /\ UNCHANGED << fine, load, pending, served >>

AcquireFine(a, c) ==
    /\ coarse = a
    /\ fine[c] = Free
    /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![c] = a]
    /\ UNCHANGED << coarse, load, pending, served >>

\* Board any waiting request into a car, respecting the bank ceiling.
Board(a, c, req) ==
    /\ coarse = a
    /\ fine[c] = a
    /\ req \in pending
    /\ TotalLoad < BankCap
    /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![c] = load[c] + 1]
    /\ pending' = pending \ {req}
    /\ served' = served \cup {req}
    /\ UNCHANGED << coarse, fine >>

ReleaseFine(a, c) ==
    /\ fine[c] = a
    /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![c] = Free]
    /\ UNCHANGED << coarse, load, pending, served >>

ReleaseCoarse(a) ==
    /\ coarse = a
    /\ coarse' = Free
    /\ UNCHANGED << fine, load, pending, served >>

Next ==
    \/ \E a \in Agents : AcquireCoarse(a)
    \/ \E a \in Agents, c \in Cars : AcquireFine(a, c)
    \/ \E a \in Agents, c \in Cars, req \in 1..MaxReq : Board(a, c, req)
    \/ \E a \in Agents, c \in Cars : ReleaseFine(a, c)
    \/ \E a \in Agents : ReleaseCoarse(a)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* The bank never carries more passengers than its fixed occupancy ceiling.    *)
WithinCapacity == TotalLoad <= BankCap
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS BankCap = 4
          MaxReq = 4
INVARIANT WithinCapacity
nl:
An elevator bank in a skyscraper has two cars ("c1", "c2") and admits waiting
passenger requests into them. Two dispatch agents ("a1", "a2") coordinate using
a hierarchical locking discipline: an agent must first acquire the coarse bank
lock, then acquire the fine lock on a specific car, and only then may it board a
request into that car. Boarding requests may be picked up and serviced in any
order — messages can be reordered — so no fixed request sequence is assumed. The
bank has a fixed total occupancy ceiling that combined boarding across both cars
must never exceed.

The system takes these steps. AcquireCoarse(a): an agent takes the free coarse
bank lock. AcquireFine(a,c): an agent holding the coarse lock takes the free fine
lock on car c. Board(a,c,req): an agent holding both the coarse lock and car c's
fine lock boards a still-waiting request req into car c, but only while the total
number of passengers already carried across both cars is strictly below the bank
ceiling. ReleaseFine(a,c): the holder of car c's fine lock releases it.
ReleaseCoarse(a): the holder of the coarse lock releases it.

Because boarding is guarded by the total-occupancy check and each board adds
exactly one passenger, the combined load can never rise above the ceiling.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the total number of passengers carried across both cars is
always less than or equal to the bank's fixed occupancy ceiling, so the bounded
capacity is never exceeded.

---- MODULE W4Od12m6p1t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

(* A blood-bank inventory tracker serialises updates to a shared record with   *)
(* lease-based ownership: a worker must hold an unexpired lease to commit the   *)
(* next update, and leases lapse as the clock advances.  Each committed update  *)
(* is stamped with the next consecutive id, so the durable record forms a       *)
(* gap-free log.  The bank's storage capacity can change at runtime.            *)

CONSTANTS MaxT, TTL, MaxId

Workers == {"w1", "w2"}
NoOne   == "none"

VARIABLES clock, holder, expiry, committed, nextId, capacity

vars == << clock, holder, expiry, committed, nextId, capacity >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ clock \in 0..MaxT
    /\ holder \in Workers \cup {NoOne}
    /\ expiry \in 0..MaxT
    /\ committed \subseteq (1..MaxId)
    /\ nextId \in 1..(MaxId + 1)
    /\ capacity \in 1..MaxId

Init ==
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ holder = NoOne
    /\ expiry = 0
    /\ committed = {}
    /\ nextId = 1
    /\ capacity = MaxId

Tick ==
    /\ clock < MaxT
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << holder, expiry, committed, nextId, capacity >>

\* Acquire the lease when it is free or has expired; stamp a fresh expiry.
Acquire(w) ==
    /\ (holder = NoOne \/ clock >= expiry)
    /\ holder' = w
    /\ expiry' = IF clock + TTL <= MaxT THEN clock + TTL ELSE MaxT
    /\ UNCHANGED << clock, committed, nextId, capacity >>

Release(w) ==
    /\ holder = w
    /\ holder' = NoOne
    /\ UNCHANGED << clock, expiry, committed, nextId, capacity >>

\* Commit the next consecutive update; requires a still-valid lease and room.
Commit(w) ==
    /\ holder = w
    /\ clock < expiry
    /\ nextId <= MaxId
    /\ Cardinality(committed) < capacity
    /\ committed' = committed \cup {nextId}
    /\ nextId' = nextId + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << clock, holder, expiry, capacity >>

\* Storage capacity is re-provisioned at runtime.
Resize(k) ==
    /\ k # capacity
    /\ capacity' = k
    /\ UNCHANGED << clock, holder, expiry, committed, nextId >>

Next ==
    \/ Tick
    \/ \E w \in Workers : Acquire(w)
    \/ \E w \in Workers : Release(w)
    \/ \E w \in Workers : Commit(w)
    \/ \E k \in 1..MaxId : Resize(k)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* No update is ever lost: the durable record is a gap-free prefix of update   *)
(* ids, so if id i is committed then its predecessor i-1 is committed too.      *)
NoLostUpdate == \A i \in committed : (i = 1) \/ ((i - 1) \in committed)
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS MaxT = 3
          TTL = 2
          MaxId = 4
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker serialises updates to one shared inventory record
using lease-based ownership with expiry. Two workers ("w1", "w2") contend for a
single lease. A worker may take the lease when it is free or has expired, and the
lease is stamped with an expiry time measured against a global clock that ticks
forward. Only a worker holding a still-valid (unexpired) lease may commit the
next update, and each committed update is stamped with the next consecutive id,
so the durable record is a gap-free log of update ids. The bank's storage
capacity can be re-provisioned at runtime.

The system takes these steps. Tick: the global clock advances by one, which can
cause a held lease to lapse. Acquire(w): a worker takes the lease when it is free
or expired, receiving a fresh expiry. Release(w): the lease holder gives up the
lease. Commit(w): the holder of a valid lease appends the next consecutive update
id to the durable record, provided the record is below its current capacity.
Resize(k): the storage capacity is changed to a new value k at runtime.

Because commits are serialised behind a single valid lease and each stamps the
next consecutive id, the durable record never develops a gap and no update is
skipped or lost.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the durable record is always a gap-free prefix of update ids —
whenever an update id i is committed, its predecessor i-1 is also committed — so
no acknowledged update to the shared record is ever lost.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od12m5p0t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

(* Access to the blood-bank's single critical cold-store is arbitrated by      *)
(* quorum voting: each of three nodes may grant its one vote to at most one     *)
(* requester, and a requester enters the critical section only after gathering  *)
(* a quorum of grants.  Any node may crash silently, losing its vote.  Because  *)
(* votes are exclusive and a quorum is a strict majority, two different nodes    *)
(* can never both assemble a quorum at the same time.                           *)

CONSTANTS Quorum, MaxCrash

Nodes == {"n1", "n2", "n3"}
NoOne == "none"

VARIABLES requesting, grant, cs, crashed

vars == << requesting, grant, cs, crashed >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ requesting \subseteq Nodes
    /\ grant \in [Nodes -> Nodes \cup {NoOne}]
    /\ cs \subseteq Nodes
    /\ crashed \subseteq Nodes

Grants(r) == {v \in Nodes : grant[v] = r}

Init ==
    /\ requesting = {}
    /\ grant = [v \in Nodes |-> NoOne]
    /\ cs = {}
    /\ crashed = {}

Request(n) ==
    /\ n \notin requesting
    /\ n \notin cs
    /\ requesting' = requesting \cup {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED << grant, cs, crashed >>

\* A live voter with a free vote grants it to a requester.
Grant(v, r) ==
    /\ v \notin crashed
    /\ grant[v] = NoOne
    /\ r \in requesting
    /\ grant' = [grant EXCEPT ![v] = r]
    /\ UNCHANGED << requesting, cs, crashed >>

\* A voter reclaims its vote from a requester that has not yet entered.
Yield(v) ==
    /\ grant[v] # NoOne
    /\ grant[v] \notin cs
    /\ grant' = [grant EXCEPT ![v] = NoOne]
    /\ UNCHANGED << requesting, cs, crashed >>

\* Enter the critical section once a quorum has been gathered.
Enter(r) ==
    /\ r \in requesting
    /\ cs = {}
    /\ Cardinality(Grants(r)) >= Quorum
    /\ cs' = {r}
    /\ requesting' = requesting \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED << grant, crashed >>

Exit(r) ==
    /\ r \in cs
    /\ cs' = {}
    /\ grant' = [v \in Nodes |-> IF grant[v] = r THEN NoOne ELSE grant[v]]
    /\ UNCHANGED << requesting, crashed >>

\* A node crashes silently, dropping the vote it may have granted.
Crash(v) ==
    /\ v \notin crashed
    /\ Cardinality(crashed) < MaxCrash
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {v}
    /\ grant' = [grant EXCEPT ![v] = NoOne]
    /\ UNCHANGED << requesting, cs >>

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Request(n)
    \/ \E v \in Nodes, r \in Nodes : Grant(v, r)
    \/ \E v \in Nodes : Yield(v)
    \/ \E r \in Nodes : Enter(r)
    \/ \E r \in Nodes : Exit(r)
    \/ \E v \in Nodes : Crash(v)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* Two distinct nodes can never both hold a quorum of grants simultaneously,   *)
(* which is what guarantees mutually exclusive access to the cold-store.        *)
QuorumExclusion ==
    \A a, b \in Nodes :
        (Cardinality(Grants(a)) >= Quorum /\ Cardinality(Grants(b)) >= Quorum)
            => a = b
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS Quorum = 2
          MaxCrash = 1
INVARIANT QuorumExclusion
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker guards access to its single critical cold-store
using quorum voting on each action. Three nodes ("n1", "n2", "n3") each hold one
vote. A node that wants the cold-store requests it; other nodes may each grant
their single vote to one requester, and a requester enters the critical section
only after it has gathered a quorum (a strict majority) of grants. At most one
participant may crash silently, which drops the vote it had granted. Votes are
exclusive: a voter that has granted its vote cannot grant it again until it
reclaims or crashes.

The system takes these steps. Request(n): a node not already requesting and not
in the critical section asks for the cold-store. Grant(v,r): a live voter v with
a free vote grants it to a requester r. Yield(v): a voter reclaims its vote from
a requester that has not yet entered the critical section. Enter(r): a requester
that has gathered a quorum of grants, and while no one else is in the critical
section, enters it and stops requesting. Exit(r): the occupant leaves the
critical section and all votes granted to it are released. Crash(v): a node
crashes silently (at most one such crash occurs) and the vote it had granted is
dropped.

Because each voter's vote is exclusive and a quorum is a strict majority, two
different nodes can never simultaneously hold a quorum of grants.

SAFETY PROPERTY: no two distinct nodes ever simultaneously hold a quorum of
grants, so the critical cold-store is accessed by at most one node at a time —
mutual exclusion of the critical resource holds.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od16m6p3t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

(* A pharmacy prescription dispenser allocates fill slots under lease-based    *)
(* ownership with expiry.  To allocate a slot a dispenser must hold that slot's *)
(* unexpired lease, and a slot's lease is exclusive.  Once a slot is allocated  *)
(* its lease is frozen to the allocating dispenser, so a second (or slow, stale)*)
(* dispenser can never re-lease and double-allocate the same slot.  Dispensers  *)
(* may be slow but never fail.  When every slot is filled a new batch resets.   *)

CONSTANTS MaxT, TTL

Slots      == {"s1", "s2"}
Dispensers == {"d1", "d2"}
NoOne      == "none"

VARIABLES clock, leaseHolder, leaseExp, allocTo

vars == << clock, leaseHolder, leaseExp, allocTo >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ clock \in 0..MaxT
    /\ leaseHolder \in [Slots -> Dispensers \cup {NoOne}]
    /\ leaseExp \in [Slots -> 0..MaxT]
    /\ allocTo \in [Slots -> Dispensers \cup {NoOne}]

Init ==
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ leaseHolder = [s \in Slots |-> NoOne]
    /\ leaseExp = [s \in Slots |-> 0]
    /\ allocTo = [s \in Slots |-> NoOne]

Tick ==
    /\ clock < MaxT
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << leaseHolder, leaseExp, allocTo >>

\* Take an unallocated slot's lease when it is free or expired.
Acquire(d, s) ==
    /\ allocTo[s] = NoOne
    /\ (leaseHolder[s] = NoOne \/ clock >= leaseExp[s])
    /\ leaseHolder' = [leaseHolder EXCEPT ![s] = d]
    /\ leaseExp' = [leaseExp EXCEPT ![s] = IF clock + TTL <= MaxT THEN clock + TTL ELSE MaxT]
    /\ UNCHANGED << clock, allocTo >>

ReleaseLease(d, s) ==
    /\ leaseHolder[s] = d
    /\ allocTo[s] = NoOne
    /\ leaseHolder' = [leaseHolder EXCEPT ![s] = NoOne]
    /\ UNCHANGED << clock, leaseExp, allocTo >>

\* Allocate the slot; only the holder of a still-valid lease may do so.
Allocate(d, s) ==
    /\ leaseHolder[s] = d
    /\ clock < leaseExp[s]
    /\ allocTo[s] = NoOne
    /\ allocTo' = [allocTo EXCEPT ![s] = d]
    /\ UNCHANGED << clock, leaseHolder, leaseExp >>

\* Start a fresh prescription batch once every slot is filled.
Reset ==
    /\ \A s \in Slots : allocTo[s] # NoOne
    /\ clock' = 0
    /\ leaseHolder' = [s \in Slots |-> NoOne]
    /\ leaseExp' = [s \in Slots |-> 0]
    /\ allocTo' = [s \in Slots |-> NoOne]

Next ==
    \/ Tick
    \/ \E d \in Dispensers, s \in Slots : Acquire(d, s)
    \/ \E d \in Dispensers, s \in Slots : ReleaseLease(d, s)
    \/ \E d \in Dispensers, s \in Slots : Allocate(d, s)
    \/ Reset

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* Every allocated slot is allocated to precisely the dispenser that holds its *)
(* lease; since the lease is exclusive and frozen after allocation, no slot is  *)
(* ever double-allocated to a second dispenser.                                 *)
AllocMatchesLease ==
    \A s \in Slots : allocTo[s] # NoOne => allocTo[s] = leaseHolder[s]
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS MaxT = 3
          TTL = 2
INVARIANT AllocMatchesLease
nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser allocates fill slots ("s1", "s2") to two
dispensing units ("d1", "d2") using lease-based ownership with expiry. To
allocate a slot a unit must first hold that slot's lease, and each slot's lease
is exclusive to a single holder. Leases carry an expiry measured against a global
clock that ticks forward, and a unit may take a slot's lease only while the slot
is unallocated and its lease is free or has expired. Once a slot is allocated,
its lease is frozen to the allocating unit and cannot be re-leased. Dispensing
units may be slow — lagging arbitrarily between acquiring a lease and allocating
— but they never fail.

The system takes these steps. Tick: the global clock advances by one, possibly
expiring a lease. Acquire(d,s): a unit takes the lease on an unallocated slot
whose lease is free or expired, receiving a fresh expiry. ReleaseLease(d,s): a
unit releases the lease on a slot it has not yet allocated. Allocate(d,s): the
holder of a slot's still-valid lease allocates that slot to itself, provided the
slot is not already allocated. Reset: once every slot is allocated, a new
prescription batch clears all slots and leases and restarts the clock.

Because allocation requires an exclusive, unexpired lease and the lease is frozen
to the allocating unit afterward, no slot can be re-leased and handed to a second
unit — the same slot is never allocated twice.

SAFETY PROPERTY: every allocated slot is allocated to exactly the dispensing unit
that holds its lease, so no slot is ever double-allocated to two different units.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od14m0p5t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

(* A wildfire drone surveillance swarm deploys retardant on targets.  A        *)
(* retardant drop is irreversible and must happen at most once per target.     *)
(* Drones use optimistic locking with retry: a drone snapshots a target's       *)
(* version, and its drop commits only if the version is still unchanged, which  *)
(* also bumps the version so any concurrent stale attempt must abort and retry. *)
(* One drone may crash silently, abandoning its in-flight attempt.              *)

CONSTANTS MaxV, MaxCrash

Targets == {"t1", "t2"}
Drones  == {"dr1", "dr2"}
NoTgt   == "none"

VARIABLES ver, drops, snapTgt, snapVer, crashed

vars == << ver, drops, snapTgt, snapVer, crashed >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ ver \in [Targets -> 0..MaxV]
    /\ drops \in [Targets -> Nat]
    /\ snapTgt \in [Drones -> Targets \cup {NoTgt}]
    /\ snapVer \in [Drones -> 0..MaxV]
    /\ crashed \subseteq Drones

Init ==
    /\ ver = [t \in Targets |-> 0]
    /\ drops = [t \in Targets |-> 0]
    /\ snapTgt = [d \in Drones |-> NoTgt]
    /\ snapVer = [d \in Drones |-> 0]
    /\ crashed = {}

\* Snapshot a not-yet-hit target's current version to attempt a drop.
Prepare(d, t) ==
    /\ d \notin crashed
    /\ snapTgt[d] = NoTgt
    /\ drops[t] = 0
    /\ snapTgt' = [snapTgt EXCEPT ![d] = t]
    /\ snapVer' = [snapVer EXCEPT ![d] = ver[t]]
    /\ UNCHANGED << ver, drops, crashed >>

\* A concurrent write bumps a target's version, invalidating stale snapshots.
Bump(t) ==
    /\ ver[t] < MaxV
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![t] = ver[t] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED << drops, snapTgt, snapVer, crashed >>

\* Commit the irreversible drop only if the optimistic snapshot still holds.
Commit(d) ==
    /\ d \notin crashed
    /\ snapTgt[d] # NoTgt
    /\ snapVer[d] = ver[snapTgt[d]]
    /\ drops[snapTgt[d]] = 0
    /\ drops' = [drops EXCEPT ![snapTgt[d]] = @ + 1]
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![snapTgt[d]] = IF ver[snapTgt[d]] < MaxV THEN @ + 1 ELSE @]
    /\ snapTgt' = [snapTgt EXCEPT ![d] = NoTgt]
    /\ UNCHANGED << snapVer, crashed >>

\* Abandon an attempt (stale version, already-hit target, or a plain retry).
Abort(d) ==
    /\ snapTgt[d] # NoTgt
    /\ snapTgt' = [snapTgt EXCEPT ![d] = NoTgt]
    /\ UNCHANGED << ver, drops, snapVer, crashed >>

Crash(d) ==
    /\ d \notin crashed
    /\ Cardinality(crashed) < MaxCrash
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {d}
    /\ snapTgt' = [snapTgt EXCEPT ![d] = NoTgt]
    /\ UNCHANGED << ver, drops, snapVer >>

Reset ==
    /\ \A t \in Targets : drops[t] >= 1
    /\ ver' = [t \in Targets |-> 0]
    /\ drops' = [t \in Targets |-> 0]
    /\ snapTgt' = [d \in Drones |-> NoTgt]
    /\ snapVer' = [d \in Drones |-> 0]
    /\ crashed' = {}

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Drones, t \in Targets : Prepare(d, t)
    \/ \E t \in Targets : Bump(t)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Commit(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Abort(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Crash(d)
    \/ Reset

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* The irreversible retardant drop happens at most once per target: no target  *)
(* is ever recorded as dropped-on more than a single time.                      *)
AtMostOnce == \A t \in Targets : drops[t] <= 1
====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS MaxV = 2
          MaxCrash = 1
INVARIANT AtMostOnce
nl:
A wildfire drone surveillance swarm deploys fire retardant on targets ("t1",
"t2"). Dropping retardant on a target is an irreversible action that must happen
at most once per target. Two drones ("dr1", "dr2") coordinate using optimistic
locking with retry: a drone snapshots a target's version number, and its drop
commits only if that version is still unchanged at commit time. A successful
commit also bumps the target's version, so any other drone still holding a stale
snapshot must abort and retry. One drone may crash silently, abandoning any
in-flight attempt.

The system takes these steps. Prepare(d,t): a live drone with no attempt in
flight snapshots the current version of a not-yet-hit target. Bump(t): a
concurrent write increments a target's version, invalidating outstanding
snapshots. Commit(d): a drone's drop commits only if its snapshot version still
matches the target's current version and the target has not been hit; this
records the drop and bumps the version. Abort(d): a drone abandons its attempt —
because its snapshot went stale, the target was already hit, or as a plain retry.
Crash(d): one drone crashes silently and drops its in-flight attempt. Reset: once
every target has been hit, a new sortie clears the state.

Because a commit requires an unchanged optimistic snapshot and is guarded by the
target being un-hit, and every commit bumps the version, no target's retardant
drop can be committed a second time.

SAFETY PROPERTY: every target records at most one retardant drop, so the
irreversible deployment action happens at most once per target.

---- MODULE W4Od11m8p1t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

(* A print shop job spooler serialises writes to one shared spool record.  Two *)
(* spooler instances share the single pool and coordinate with hierarchical     *)
(* locks: an instance must hold the coarse spool lock before it can take the     *)
(* fine record lock, and only then may it advance the record's version.  The     *)
(* record version only ever increases, and a version is acknowledged to a client *)
(* only once it is committed, so an acknowledged update is never lost.           *)

CONSTANT MaxVer

Instances == {"spA", "spB"}
Free      == "free"

VARIABLES coarse, fine, record, acked

vars == << coarse, fine, record, acked >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ coarse \in Instances \cup {Free}
    /\ fine \in Instances \cup {Free}
    /\ record \in 0..MaxVer
    /\ acked \subseteq (1..MaxVer)

Init ==
    /\ coarse = Free
    /\ fine = Free
    /\ record = 0
    /\ acked = {}

AcquireCoarse(i) ==
    /\ coarse = Free
    /\ coarse' = i
    /\ UNCHANGED << fine, record, acked >>

AcquireFine(i) ==
    /\ coarse = i
    /\ fine = Free
    /\ fine' = i
    /\ UNCHANGED << coarse, record, acked >>

\* Advance the shared record; requires both locks in the hierarchy.
Write(i) ==
    /\ coarse = i
    /\ fine = i
    /\ record < MaxVer
    /\ record' = record + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << coarse, fine, acked >>

\* Acknowledge a committed version back to a client.
Ack(v) ==
    /\ v <= record
    /\ v >= 1
    /\ v \notin acked
    /\ acked' = acked \cup {v}
    /\ UNCHANGED << coarse, fine, record >>

ReleaseFine(i) ==
    /\ fine = i
    /\ fine' = Free
    /\ UNCHANGED << coarse, record, acked >>

ReleaseCoarse(i) ==
    /\ coarse = i
    /\ coarse' = Free
    /\ UNCHANGED << fine, record, acked >>

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Instances : AcquireCoarse(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : AcquireFine(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Write(i)
    \/ \E v \in 1..MaxVer : Ack(v)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : ReleaseFine(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : ReleaseCoarse(i)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* No acknowledged update is ever lost: every version acknowledged to a client *)
(* is still reflected in the shared record, whose version never regresses.      *)
NoLostUpdate == \A v \in acked : v <= record
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANT MaxVer = 4
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A print shop job spooler serialises writes to one shared spool record. Two
spooler instances ("spA", "spB") share the single spool pool and coordinate using
hierarchical locks (coarse then fine): an instance must first hold the coarse
spool lock, then acquire the fine record lock, and only while holding both may it
advance the record's version. The shared record version only ever increases, and
a version is acknowledged back to a client only once it has been committed.

The system takes these steps. AcquireCoarse(i): an instance takes the free coarse
spool lock. AcquireFine(i): an instance holding the coarse lock takes the free
fine record lock. Write(i): an instance holding both locks advances the shared
record version by one. Ack(v): a version v that has been committed (is no greater
than the current record version) is acknowledged to a client. ReleaseFine(i): the
fine lock holder releases it. ReleaseCoarse(i): the coarse lock holder releases
it.

Because writes only ever increase the record version and acknowledgements are
issued only for already-committed versions, no acknowledged update can later be
lost or overwritten to a smaller value.

SAFETY PROPERTY: every version acknowledged to a client is always less than or
equal to the current shared record version, so no acknowledged update to the
shared record is ever lost.

---- MODULE W4Od17m0p6t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

(* An airport baggage router lets router nodes commit routing decisions under   *)
(* optimistic locking.  A node becomes authorized by snapshotting the routing    *)
(* table's current version; only an authorized node may route a bag.  Any        *)
(* configuration change invalidates the table version and de-authorizes every    *)
(* node, so a node still carrying a stale snapshot is no longer authorized and    *)
(* must re-snapshot.  Bag messages may be routed in any order (reordered).        *)

CONSTANTS MaxVer, MaxMsg

Routers == {"r1", "r2", "r3"}

VARIABLES ver, authorized, snap, pending, routed

vars == << ver, authorized, snap, pending, routed >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ ver \in 0..MaxVer
    /\ authorized \subseteq Routers
    /\ snap \in [Routers -> 0..MaxVer]
    /\ pending \subseteq (1..MaxMsg)
    /\ routed \subseteq (1..MaxMsg)

Init ==
    /\ ver = 0
    /\ authorized = {}
    /\ snap = [r \in Routers |-> 0]
    /\ pending = 1..MaxMsg
    /\ routed = {}

\* Snapshot the current table version and become authorized.
Authorize(r) ==
    /\ r \notin authorized
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![r] = ver]
    /\ authorized' = authorized \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED << ver, pending, routed >>

\* A reconfiguration bumps the version and de-authorizes all nodes at once.
Invalidate ==
    /\ ver < MaxVer
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ authorized' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED << snap, pending, routed >>

\* A node voluntarily drops its authorization.
Deauthorize(r) ==
    /\ r \in authorized
    /\ authorized' = authorized \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED << ver, snap, pending, routed >>

\* An authorized node routes any still-pending bag (order is arbitrary).
Route(r, msg) ==
    /\ r \in authorized
    /\ msg \in pending
    /\ pending' = pending \ {msg}
    /\ routed' = routed \cup {msg}
    /\ UNCHANGED << ver, authorized, snap >>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Routers : Authorize(r)
    \/ Invalidate
    \/ \E r \in Routers : Deauthorize(r)
    \/ \E r \in Routers, msg \in 1..MaxMsg : Route(r, msg)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* No stale node is ever treated as authorized: every authorized node holds a   *)
(* snapshot equal to the current table version, so routing is never performed    *)
(* by a stale (or never-authorized) participant.                                 *)
AuthorizedAreCurrent == \A r \in authorized : snap[r] = ver
====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS MaxVer = 3
          MaxMsg = 4
INVARIANT AuthorizedAreCurrent
nl:
An airport baggage router routes bags by having router nodes ("r1", "r2", "r3")
commit routing decisions under optimistic locking with retry. A node becomes
authorized by snapshotting the routing table's current version; only an
authorized node may route a bag. Any configuration change invalidates the table
by bumping its version and de-authorizing every node at once, so a node still
holding a stale snapshot is no longer authorized and must re-snapshot before it
can act again. Bag messages may be routed in any order — messages can be
reordered — so no fixed processing sequence is assumed.

The system takes these steps. Authorize(r): a node snapshots the current table
version and joins the authorized set. Invalidate: a reconfiguration increments
the table version and clears the authorized set, making every outstanding
snapshot stale. Deauthorize(r): a node voluntarily drops its authorization.
Route(r,msg): an authorized node routes any still-pending bag, chosen in
arbitrary order, moving it from pending to routed.

Because every version bump clears the authorized set and authorization requires a
fresh snapshot of the current version, a node whose snapshot has gone stale is
never a member of the authorized set and can never route a bag.

SAFETY PROPERTY: every authorized node holds a snapshot equal to the current
table version, so no stale or unauthorized participant ever performs a routing
action.

---- MODULE W4Od11m7p3t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

(* A print shop job spooler assigns print slots through per-slot compare-and-   *)
(* swap registers.  A worker allocates a requested slot only by a successful     *)
(* CAS from the empty owner to itself; a CAS against an already-owned slot fails *)
(* and the request is retried elsewhere.  The spool's capacity changes at        *)
(* runtime.  Because each allocation is one successful CAS on a distinct empty    *)
(* slot, the count of allocation events equals the number of owned slots.        *)

CONSTANT MaxCap

Slots   == {"j1", "j2", "j3"}
Workers == {"wk1", "wk2"}
Empty   == "empty"

VARIABLES owner, allocCount, capacity, queue

vars == << owner, allocCount, capacity, queue >>

Owned == {s \in Slots : owner[s] # Empty}

TypeOK ==
    /\ owner \in [Slots -> Workers \cup {Empty}]
    /\ allocCount \in Nat
    /\ capacity \in 1..MaxCap
    /\ queue \subseteq Slots

Init ==
    /\ owner = [s \in Slots |-> Empty]
    /\ allocCount = 0
    /\ capacity = MaxCap
    /\ queue = {}

Request(s) ==
    /\ s \notin queue
    /\ owner[s] = Empty
    /\ queue' = queue \cup {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED << owner, allocCount, capacity >>

\* Successful CAS: claim a requested, still-empty slot while under capacity.
CAS(w, s) ==
    /\ s \in queue
    /\ owner[s] = Empty
    /\ Cardinality(Owned) < capacity
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = w]
    /\ allocCount' = allocCount + 1
    /\ queue' = queue \ {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED capacity

\* Failed CAS: the slot was taken meanwhile; drop the request (retry elsewhere).
Retry(s) ==
    /\ s \in queue
    /\ owner[s] # Empty
    /\ queue' = queue \ {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED << owner, allocCount, capacity >>

Resize(k) ==
    /\ k # capacity
    /\ capacity' = k
    /\ UNCHANGED << owner, allocCount, queue >>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Slots : Request(s)
    \/ \E w \in Workers, s \in Slots : CAS(w, s)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : Retry(s)
    \/ \E k \in 1..MaxCap : Resize(k)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* No slot is ever allocated twice: the number of successful allocation events *)
(* equals the number of distinct owned slots, so each owned slot was claimed by  *)
(* exactly one CAS.                                                              *)
NoDoubleAllocation == allocCount = Cardinality(Owned)
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANT MaxCap = 3
INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation
nl:
A print shop job spooler assigns print slots ("j1", "j2", "j3") to workers
("wk1", "wk2") using a compare-and-swap register per slot. A worker allocates a
requested slot only through a successful CAS that swaps the slot's owner from
empty to itself; a CAS attempted against a slot that is already owned fails, and
that request is retried elsewhere. The spool's capacity — the number of slots
that may be simultaneously owned — changes at runtime.

The system takes these steps. Request(s): an empty, not-yet-requested slot is put
on the request queue. CAS(w,s): a worker performs a successful compare-and-swap,
claiming a requested slot that is still empty while the number of owned slots is
below the current capacity; this records one allocation event. Retry(s): a CAS
that finds its slot already owned fails, so the request is dropped and retried.
Resize(k): the capacity is changed to a new value k at runtime.

Because a slot can be claimed only while empty and each successful CAS fills a
distinct empty slot, the running count of allocation events stays equal to the
number of owned slots — no slot is ever allocated a second time.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of successful allocation events always equals the
number of distinct owned slots, so no slot is ever double-allocated.

EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

(* A smart-home door lock network permanently commissions door locks.  Locking  *)
(* in a door's master key is an irreversible action that must happen at most     *)
(* once per door.  The network runs epoch-numbered reconfiguration: a door must  *)
(* be provisioned in the CURRENT epoch to be commissioned, and each new epoch     *)
(* invalidates prior provisioning.  A door may be slow (lagging, needing to       *)
(* re-provision after an epoch change) but never fails.  Every commissioning is   *)
(* appended to an audit log that must never name a door twice.                    *)

CONSTANT MaxEpoch

Doors == {"front", "back"}

VARIABLES epoch, provEpoch, commissioned, auditLog

vars == << epoch, provEpoch, commissioned, auditLog >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ provEpoch \in [Doors -> 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ commissioned \subseteq Doors
    /\ auditLog \in Seq(Doors)

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ provEpoch = [d \in Doors |-> 0]
    /\ commissioned = {}
    /\ auditLog = << >>

\* Reconfiguration advances the epoch, staling all prior provisioning.
Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << provEpoch, commissioned, auditLog >>

\* Provision a door in the current epoch (a slow door may re-provision).
Provision(d) ==
    /\ provEpoch[d] # epoch
    /\ provEpoch' = [provEpoch EXCEPT ![d] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, commissioned, auditLog >>

Deprovision(d) ==
    /\ provEpoch[d] = epoch
    /\ d \notin commissioned
    /\ provEpoch' = [provEpoch EXCEPT ![d] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, commissioned, auditLog >>

\* Irreversibly commission a door; requires current-epoch provisioning.
Commission(d) ==
    /\ d \notin commissioned
    /\ provEpoch[d] = epoch
    /\ epoch > 0
    /\ commissioned' = commissioned \cup {d}
    /\ auditLog' = Append(auditLog, d)
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, provEpoch >>

\* Once every door is commissioned, a fresh install cycle resets the network.
Reset ==
    /\ \A d \in Doors : d \in commissioned
    /\ epoch' = 0
    /\ provEpoch' = [d \in Doors |-> 0]
    /\ commissioned' = {}
    /\ auditLog' = << >>

Next ==
    \/ Reconfigure
    \/ \E d \in Doors : Provision(d)
    \/ \E d \in Doors : Deprovision(d)
    \/ \E d \in Doors : Commission(d)
    \/ Reset

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* The irreversible commissioning happens at most once per door: no door is     *)
(* ever named twice in the audit log.                                           *)
CommissionAtMostOnce ==
    \A i, j \in 1..Len(auditLog) : (auditLog[i] = auditLog[j]) => (i = j)
====

CONSTANT MaxEpoch = 3
INVARIANT CommissionAtMostOnce
nl:
A smart-home door lock network permanently commissions door locks ("front",
"back"). Commissioning a door — locking in its master key — is an irreversible
action that must happen at most once per door. The network runs epoch-numbered
reconfiguration: a door must be provisioned in the current epoch before it can be
commissioned, and advancing to a new epoch invalidates all prior provisioning. A
door may be slow — lagging behind, so that after an epoch change it must
re-provision before acting — but it never fails. Every commissioning is appended
to an audit log that must never name the same door twice.

The system takes these steps. Reconfigure: the network advances the epoch,
making every door's prior provisioning stale. Provision(d): a door is provisioned
in the current epoch; a slow door whose provisioning went stale may re-provision.
Deprovision(d): a not-yet-commissioned door's current-epoch provisioning is
cleared. Commission(d): a door provisioned in the current epoch is irreversibly
commissioned and appended to the audit log, provided it has not been commissioned
before. Reset: once every door is commissioned, a fresh install cycle resets the
network.

Because commissioning is guarded by the door not already being commissioned and
each commissioning appends exactly one audit entry, no door is ever commissioned
or logged a second time.

SAFETY PROPERTY: no door is ever named more than once in the commissioning audit
log, so the irreversible commissioning action happens at most once per door.

EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

(* A pharmacy prescription dispenser grants a single dispensing authorization    *)
(* at a time under optimistic locking.  A dispenser is authorized by stamping    *)
(* the current authority version onto itself; only the holder whose stamp still  *)
(* matches the authority version may dispense.  A revocation bumps the authority  *)
(* version and clears the holder, so any leftover stamp is stale.  One dispenser  *)
(* may crash silently, losing the authorization if it held it.                   *)

CONSTANTS MaxVer, MaxDisp, MaxCrash

Dispensers == {"dx", "dy", "dz"}
NoOne      == "none"

VARIABLES authVer, holder, holderVer, dispensed, crashed

vars == << authVer, holder, holderVer, dispensed, crashed >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ authVer \in 0..MaxVer
    /\ holder \in Dispensers \cup {NoOne}
    /\ holderVer \in 0..MaxVer
    /\ dispensed \in 0..MaxDisp
    /\ crashed \subseteq Dispensers

Init ==
    /\ authVer = 0
    /\ holder = NoOne
    /\ holderVer = 0
    /\ dispensed = 0
    /\ crashed = {}

\* Grant authorization, stamping the current authority version onto the holder.
Authorize(d) ==
    /\ holder = NoOne
    /\ d \notin crashed
    /\ holder' = d
    /\ holderVer' = authVer
    /\ UNCHANGED << authVer, dispensed, crashed >>

\* Revoke: bump the authority version and clear the holder in one atomic step.
Revoke ==
    /\ holder # NoOne
    /\ authVer' = IF authVer < MaxVer THEN authVer + 1 ELSE authVer
    /\ holder' = NoOne
    /\ UNCHANGED << holderVer, dispensed, crashed >>

\* Release authorization voluntarily without bumping the version.
Release ==
    /\ holder # NoOne
    /\ holder' = NoOne
    /\ UNCHANGED << authVer, holderVer, dispensed, crashed >>

\* Only the holder whose stamp is current may dispense.
Dispense(d) ==
    /\ holder = d
    /\ holderVer = authVer
    /\ d \notin crashed
    /\ dispensed < MaxDisp
    /\ dispensed' = dispensed + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << authVer, holder, holderVer, crashed >>

Crash(d) ==
    /\ d \notin crashed
    /\ Cardinality(crashed) < MaxCrash
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {d}
    /\ holder' = IF holder = d THEN NoOne ELSE holder
    /\ UNCHANGED << authVer, holderVer, dispensed >>

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Dispensers : Authorize(d)
    \/ Revoke
    \/ Release
    \/ \E d \in Dispensers : Dispense(d)
    \/ \E d \in Dispensers : Crash(d)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* The current holder's authorization stamp always matches the live authority   *)
(* version, so no stale or unauthorized dispenser is ever treated as the holder  *)
(* and allowed to dispense.                                                      *)
HolderIsCurrent == holder # NoOne => holderVer = authVer
====

INVARIANT HolderIsCurrent
nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser grants a single dispensing authorization at a
time under optimistic locking with retry. Dispensers ("dx", "dy", "dz") contend
for the authorization. A dispenser becomes authorized by stamping the current
authority version onto itself; only the holder whose stamp still matches the live
authority version may dispense a prescription. A revocation bumps the authority
version and clears the holder in one atomic step, so any leftover stamp from a
former holder is stale. At most one dispenser may crash silently, and a crashed
dispenser loses the authorization if it was holding it.

The system takes these steps. Authorize(d): when there is no holder, a live
dispenser is granted authorization and stamped with the current authority
version. Revoke: the current holder is cleared and the authority version is
bumped, staling any old stamp. Release: the current holder voluntarily gives up
authorization without bumping the version. Dispense(d): the holder whose stamp
matches the live authority version dispenses a prescription. Crash(d): one
dispenser crashes silently, releasing the authorization if it held it.

Because revocation clears the holder in the same step that bumps the version,
there is never a moment where a stale-stamped or unauthorized dispenser is
recorded as the holder.

SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever there is a holder, its authorization stamp equals the
current authority version, so no stale or unauthorized participant is ever
allowed to dispense.

---- MODULE W4Od13m4p1t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

(* A vending machine network feeds restock updates through one bounded work     *)
(* queue with backpressure: an update is admitted only when the queue has room   *)
(* below its current capacity, and the consumer applies queued updates to the    *)
(* inventory record.  Every admitted update is always either still queued or     *)
(* already applied -- none is ever dropped -- so no update is lost.  The queue    *)
(* capacity changes at runtime.                                                  *)

CONSTANT MaxId

VARIABLES admitted, queue, applied, capacity, nextId

vars == << admitted, queue, applied, capacity, nextId >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ admitted \subseteq (1..MaxId)
    /\ queue \subseteq (1..MaxId)
    /\ applied \subseteq (1..MaxId)
    /\ capacity \in 1..MaxId
    /\ nextId \in 1..(MaxId + 1)

Init ==
    /\ admitted = {}
    /\ queue = {}
    /\ applied = {}
    /\ capacity = MaxId
    /\ nextId = 1

\* Admit the next update only if the bounded queue has room (backpressure).
Admit ==
    /\ nextId <= MaxId
    /\ Cardinality(queue) < capacity
    /\ admitted' = admitted \cup {nextId}
    /\ queue' = queue \cup {nextId}
    /\ nextId' = nextId + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << applied, capacity >>

\* Consume a queued update and apply it to the inventory record.
Apply(id) ==
    /\ id \in queue
    /\ queue' = queue \ {id}
    /\ applied' = applied \cup {id}
    /\ UNCHANGED << admitted, capacity, nextId >>

\* Re-provision the queue capacity at runtime.
Resize(k) ==
    /\ k # capacity
    /\ capacity' = k
    /\ UNCHANGED << admitted, queue, applied, nextId >>

\* Start a fresh batch once every admitted update has drained and applied.
Reset ==
    /\ queue = {}
    /\ nextId > MaxId
    /\ admitted' = {}
    /\ queue' = {}
    /\ applied' = {}
    /\ capacity' = MaxId
    /\ nextId' = 1

Next ==
    \/ Admit
    \/ \E id \in 1..MaxId : Apply(id)
    \/ \E k \in 1..MaxId : Resize(k)
    \/ Reset

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* No update is ever lost: every admitted update is either still in the queue   *)
(* or already applied to the inventory record.                                  *)
NoLostUpdate == admitted = (queue \cup applied)
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANT MaxId = 4
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A vending machine network feeds restock updates through a single bounded work
queue with backpressure. Updates are numbered consecutively. An update is
admitted into the system only when the queue currently holds fewer entries than
its capacity (this is the backpressure: a full queue refuses new work). A
consumer applies queued updates to the shared inventory record. Every admitted
update is always either still waiting in the queue or already applied, and none
is ever silently dropped. The queue's capacity changes at runtime.

The system takes these steps. Admit: the next consecutive update is admitted and
enqueued, but only while the queue is below its current capacity. Apply(id): the
consumer removes a queued update from the queue and records it as applied to the
inventory record. Resize(k): the queue capacity is changed to a new value k at
runtime. Reset: once the queue has fully drained and all updates have been
admitted, a fresh restock batch resets the system.

Because admission adds an update to both the admitted set and the queue, and
applying moves it from the queue to the applied set without ever discarding it,
the admitted set always equals the union of the queued and applied updates.

SAFETY PROPERTY: every admitted update is always either still in the queue or
already applied to the inventory record, so no admitted update is ever lost.
